concurrency_note: ratchet check is a single-pass fold over checked-in test results (the scorecard's pass_set) and epic-doc contract-definition hashes at a fixed scorecard/journal snapshot. There is no concurrent/racing-writer channel in the artifact to evade; the tamper concern (a racing edit of the journal itself) is addressed by the append-only hash chain, not by a concurrency seed (see assumptions).

authority_boundary.proves: over a target repo's checked-in test scorecard + epic docs (docs/epics/**/*.md and *.json), a contract/invariant whose stable-ID block content changed since it entered the high-water mark is reported as weakened_contracts, one that no longer resolves under the configured epic_docs scan root is reported as removed_contracts, and a high-water test case no longer in the pass_set is reported as missing_tests; the high-water mark itself is derived from a hash-chained journal that fails closed on tamper; additionally (#206), a test function annotated `@cw-trace verifies <ID>` whose body hash changed since entering the high-water mark is reported as weakened_verifier_tests, and one whose ref vanished as removed_verifier_tests — REPORT-ONLY findings unless check is invoked with --gate-verifier-tests; and — as of #295 — that the contract-hash high-water actually MEASURED something: an epic whose ID-bearing artifacts carry content but yield zero parseable ids reports contract_measurement.status=error and blocks, rather than holding 'contracts cannot be weakened' vacuously over an empty set; and — as of #289 — that the pass-set was actually MEASURED: a dead suite command or a 0-collection run reports suite_measurement error in the hard tier rather than an empty pass-set reading as 'ratchet: OK'
authority_boundary.artifact: a target repo working tree: its ratchet state (docs/quality/ratchet.json config, ratchet-journal.jsonl hash chain, ratchet-scorecard.json) plus the epic-doc contract definitions under the configured epic_docs root
assumptions: contract-definition hashing normalizes only TRAILING per-line whitespace and surrounding blank lines (hash_markdown_defs rstrip/strip) — a pure trailing/surrounding-blank reformat does NOT read as weakening, but a wording change to the REQUIRES/ENSURES text does; note that inserting INTERNAL blank lines inside a block is not normalized and would read as a change

structured JSON contract blocks (models/*.json objects carrying an ID_RE-matching "id") are hashed via walk_json_ids exactly like markdown-declared blocks — the JSON declaration path is not a coverage gap

the docs/epics/**/justifications/ subtree is EXCLUDED by design (chief_wiggum.trace_links.is_justification_path): a waiver's own "id" names the CTR/INV it waives and must never be misread as a new declaration, so a contract block placed there is a certified NON-coverage boundary, not a detectable definition

the journal is an append-only stable_hash chain; load_journal raises TamperError (fail-closed, exit 4) on any broken link, so the high-water mark cannot be silently lowered by editing state — this is exercised by tests/test_ratchet.py::test_journal_tamper_fails_closed rather than by a seed_class trial (a tamper is an exit-4 fail-closed, not a findings-based fire/no-fire outcome)
the pass_set is only meaningful for suites the target repo actually configures and runs; a test channel with no configured suite contributes no high-water cases to protect

verifier-test hashing (#206) covers the annotated test function's OWN source span only: assertions relocated into a shared helper/fixture the test calls are a certified NON-coverage boundary (rt-verifier-config-indirection-01)

verifier annotations are read from Python comment tokens and function docstrings only — an annotation inside a string literal (e.g. a test that WRITES an annotated fixture) never pins the writing test; documentation formats (.md/.rst/.txt) are out of scope by design (syntax examples, not tests)
only Python is extracted in v1; a verifies annotation in any other language is surfaced by score as verifier_unscanned, never silently dropped (rt-verifier-sampling-gap-01)

verifier-test hashing keys refs by class-qualified name; a duplicate qualified name (function redefined under a conditional, a shadowed class) is ambiguous and surfaced as unscanned + refused, never recorded as a single overwritten hash (#206 soundness review)

amending a CONTRACT never silently blesses its verifier tests' changed bodies — a changed verifier body must be named with --amend-verifier explicitly or the amend is refused, so a body rewrite cannot ride along on a contract-wording amend (channel C1c)

C# suites are measured from TRX (`dotnet test --logger trx`): only outcome="Passed" counts (Failed/Error/Timeout/Aborted/Inconclusive/NotExecuted do not), case IDs are ClassName::LocalName resolved via <TestDefinitions>, and a suite's `report` may name a DIRECTORY — every *.trx under it is parsed, because `dotnet test` writes one per test project and reading a single file would silently undercount a solution. A TRX class maps to a source file only when exactly one tracked <ClassName>.cs exists under the suite cwd; ambiguous or absent matches stay unresolved and are surfaced as test_files_unresolved, never guessed

a pass-set case leaves the high-water mark ONLY via a journaled record --retire-case carrying a reason and a non-past expiry, refused for a case that is still passing in the current scorecard (so cases cannot be pre-emptively retired before being broken) and for a case absent from the high-water mark; the waiver is a chain-linked journal record, so quarantine is tamper-evident and attributable, and an expired or unparseable-expiry entry STOPS waiving and re-enters missing_tests (chief-wiggum#278). What the gate does NOT prove: that a quarantine was justified — only that it was journaled, attributed, bounded by an expiry, and surfaced in check/highwater/status.
what this does NOT prove: that the contracts the ratchet hashed are the RIGHT contracts — only that a silently-unparseable epic can no longer be mistaken for one with nothing to weaken

a case may leave the pass-set ONLY via a journaled retirement (#278 quarantine, or #290 permanent removal with an explicit owner and no expiry). A case that simply vanishes from the suite with no journal entry behind it still fires missing_tests — verified empirically and pinned by tests/test_ratchet.py::test_a_case_vanishing_without_a_journal_entry_still_fires. What this does NOT prove: that a recorded retirement was JUSTIFIED — only that it was journaled, attributed to a named owner, and surfaced separately from quarantines

junit reports are pre-cleared before a run (as trx already was) — before #289 a STALE report left over from an earlier run, combined with a suite command that no longer executed, fabricated a non-zero pass count from the previous run's numbers. The scorecard's suite_measurement denominator makes the scanned-case count visible even when green

This is a write-path robustness fix and a read-path error-shape fix: NO finding class added or narrowed, no threshold moved, no change to any subcommand's exit semantics on a well-formed journal. The new guards are mutation-tested (3/3: separator suppressed, separator written into an empty journal, and cmd_record reverted to its own inline append - the last one covers the two-call-site drift that made this defect possible). Extended after adversarial review of the same change: the separator decision was being made from a read_text() snapshot taken before the file was opened, which is a stale decision - a competing or crashed writer can leave an unterminated tail in that window, and the append would then fuse onto it while believing the file was terminated, reintroducing the very bug. The terminator is now probed as the last byte of the handle the record is written through. That narrows the window rather than closing it (true atomicity needs a lock the journal has never taken, and the dominant pre-existing hazard is two writers computing prev from the same snapshot, which forks the chain). Review also found that the read-side hardening was incomplete: a corrupt line which is VALID JSON but not an object (null, [], a bare string or number, plausible from a hand edit or a third-party tool) parsed cleanly and then died on rec.items() with an unhandled AttributeError at EXIT 1 - which is VIOLATED, the code for a real quality regression. A corrupt instrument reading as a shrunken pass-set is precisely the state confusion #289 exists to prevent, and it was inconsistent with the exit 4 an invalid-JSON line already produced. load_journal now rejects any non-object record as tamper. Still no finding class added or narrowed and no change to any subcommand's exit semantics on a well-formed journal; the 9 seeded trials and the clean-corpus run were re-executed live again against this code, and the new guards are mutation-tested 4/4 (non-object line accepted, terminator probed from a stale snapshot, separator suppressed, separator written into an empty journal).
